The country’s top court announces expedited hearing of appeals surrounding “stripping or disabling” law and schedule for oral arguments
The country's leader-elect has filed papers with the Supreme Court asking for a suspension of the divestment cutoff to buy time for political negotiations after taking office.
The country's judiciary opposes the leader-elect's request to delay execution in a Supreme Court filing and urges the law to remain on schedule
The country's top court held oral arguments on the controversial law, with a majority of judges skeptical of the platform's claims.

The country's administrative authorities have publicly stated that they will not immediately enforce the relevant prohibition laws on the legal effective date and will transfer the enforcement responsibility to the new government.
The country’s Supreme Court rejected the platform’s application for an emergency injunction and kept the “stripping or banning” law from taking effect as scheduled.
The short video platform resumed services to users after a brief interruption in the country amid banning laws taking effect, while app stores continue to remove them
The country’s new leader signed an executive order to extend the ban on the short video platform for a period of time to obtain a disposal window.
The country’s new leader signed an executive order to launch the establishment of a sovereign wealth fund and publicly stated that the fund may be used to acquire the short video platform
Several civil rights and free speech organizations jointly submitted an amicus brief to the highest judicial body urging to prevent the ban from taking effect.
Leader-elect makes first public endorsement of Platform X's continued operations at rally, reveals billions of views during campaign
The judiciary files a document with the top judicial body, formally urging the rejection of the incoming leader's request to delay the ban and emphasizing that the platform is a tool for espionage

Platform X invoked the freedom of speech clause for the first time to defend, pointing out that the legislation did not ban other applications owned by foreign countries, indicating that the real target was its social media content rather than data.

The creator community has become anxious due to interruptions in reward programs and live streaming income. Some people have begun to turn to competing products such as graphic applications and comparison video platforms.
The court made a final ruling to uphold the ban on the platform. All the justices unanimously supported it, and the platform immediately stopped serving in the country.
The elected leader's government enters talks with a technology company and outside investor group to take over the platform's global operations
Leaders publicly stated that they are negotiating with multiple parties to acquire the platform and said they would make a decision on the sale within dozens of days.
Leaders signed an executive order instructing relevant agencies to establish a sovereign wealth fund within a year, saying it may be used to acquire the platform

Regulatory authorities sent letters to the two major app stores, promising not to pursue legal liability for hosting or distributing the platform during the extension period
The platform has been re-listed. If the government and the platform fail to reach an agreement on time, they may face delisting again.
